After a genuine adversarial search I could not find a sequence on which the revised Lean law (work/reviews/lem-transport-angle-interval-reviewer-input-statement.lean.txt, lines 19-24) and the printed lemma (source excerpt lines 3-7) disagree, and no clause of the Lean statement is weaker than the printed text.

2. Step hypothesis. Printed "|θ_{i+1}−θ_i|<π" = Lean `∀ i : Fin N, |θ i.succ - θ i.castSucc| < π`. I kernel-checked `(i.castSucc).val = i.val` and `(i.succ).val = i.val + 1`, so this is exactly |θ_{i+1} − θ_i| < π for i = 0..N−1, with the same strict inequality (`open Real`, so `π = Real.pi`). It appears only as the antecedent of the forward conjunct (line 22), exactly where the printed "If … has …" places it.
3. Unit directions. `unitDir θ := (Real.cos θ, Real.sin θ) : Plane` with `Plane := ℝ × ℝ` (TransportAngleInterval.lean:32, Polygon.lean:13); conjunct 1 (line 20) records this definitionally. Matches "unit directions".
4. Closed semicircle. `InClosedSemicircle θ := ∃ v : Plane, planeDot v v = 1 ∧ ∀ i, 0 ≤ planeDot v (unitDir (θ i))` (TransportAngleInterval.lean:36-37), `planeDot u v := u.1*v.1 + u.2*v.2` (EuclideanPlane.lean:27). A closed semicircle of the unit circle is exactly {u : |u| = 1, ⟨u,v⟩ ≥ 0} for a unit v, and unitDir(θ i) is on the unit circle, so this is exactly "all unit directions lie in a closed semicircle" with the boundary included (≤, not <). Conjunct 2 (line 21) adds the angular equivalence `∃ α, ∀ i, 0 ≤ cos (θ i − α)`; that is extra content (stronger than source), not a weakening.
5. Interval of length π. Lean `∃ c, ∀ i, c ≤ θ i ∧ θ i ≤ c + π` (closed [c, c+π]). Forward direction: the closed reading is the only one under which the printed lemma is true, and it is the one the printed proof uses ("intervals [α+2πk, α+π+2πk]"); I kernel-checked that θ = (0, π/2, π) satisfies the Lean step hypothesis and InClosedSemicircle (v = (0,1)), lies in [0,π], and lies in NO open interval of length π. Converse direction: the closed-interval hypothesis is the weakest possible, so Lean's converse (line 24) is the strongest reading and implies every open/half-open variant.

Converse = conjunct 4 (line 24), hypothesis = containment only, for every θ : Fin (N+1) → ℝ. The printed "Conversely, containment of all entries in such an interval puts their unit directions in a closed semicircle" mentions no step hypothesis, so this matches; under a reading where the converse inherits the step hypothesis Lean would be stronger, never weaker. The round-1 objection is resolved.
